transcript.text: theres a funny smell from my oven when its on

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. A 'funny smell' when an oven is on can be harmless, but because you haven't specified the type yet, we need to rule out a serious electrical issue first. The most critical possibility is that the mains terminal block (where the power cable connects to the back of the oven) is overheating due to a loose or damaged connection. 1. Switch off the oven and isolate it at the wall switch or consumer unit.
2. Look carefully at the back of the oven where the main power cable enters. Do you see any charring, melting, blackening, or white powdery residue on the plastic block or the cable insulation?
3. Does the smell seem to come from that specific area at the back, or is it coming from inside the cooking cavity? If you see any damage or if the smell is distinctly like burning plastic/electrical wiring, STOP using the oven immediately and call a qualified engineer. Do not attempt to repair the mains connection yourself. If there is no visible damage at the back and the smell seems more like burnt food or dust, it may be normal residue burn-off or spillage. Please let me know what you find.

I can't look at the back, the cooker's too heavy to pull out on my own. The smell is more like hot plastic or electrical and seems to come from behind/below, not inside the oven. The cooker switch on the wall also looks a bit brown at one corner and felt warm.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The warm, browned wall switch and the hot-plastic smell coming from behind/below point to an overheating electrical connection. This is most likely either the oven's internal mains terminal block where the cable enters, or the wall-mounted cooker isolator switch itself. Both are serious fire hazards caused by high resistance (a loose or degraded contact). Because this involves fixed mains wiring and a component that has already shown signs of thermal damage, you must not use the appliance again. Do not attempt to pull the heavy cooker out yourself to inspect further; the weight and risk of damaging the cable or connection make it unsafe for a non-professional. Please switch off the oven at the wall isolator (if safe to do so without touching hot parts) or turn off the circuit at your consumer unit/fuse box. You will need a qualified electrician or gas-safe registered engineer (depending on whether it is electric or gas, though 'hot plastic' usually implies electric) to inspect and repair the connection. Do not try to use the oven until this has been professionally checked.
